name: Dipolog City Scholarship and Educational Financial Assistance Program
provider: City Government of Dipolog — Scholarship Program Management Unit (SPMU), City Mayor's Office
forWho: Incoming college students who have lived in Dipolog City for at least 5 years, with a barangay indigency certification and a certificate of good moral character from their school. The SY 2025–2026 call also asked for a minimum 85% average in Senior High School.
howToApply: For the SY 2025–2026 cycle, applicants submitted a letter of intent, photocopy of the Senior High School card (1st and 2nd semester), Certificate of Good Moral Character, Barangay Residency Certification (at least 5 years), Indigency Certification and one 2x2 photo to the SPMU, 3rd Floor, Dipolog City Hall, then took a scholarship exam. Ask the SPMU or call the City Mayor's Office at (065) 212-2484 for the current cycle's requirements.
timing: Annual. The SY 2025–2026 cycle closed on April 16, 2025, with the exam on April 27, 2025. Details come from a reposted city announcement, and no newer cycle was found online. Watch the City Government's official announcements.

name: CSWDO Aid to Individuals in Crisis Situation (AICS) — Medical and Burial Assistance
provider: City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO), City Government of Dipolog
forWho: Indigent residents of Dipolog City in a crisis situation who need medical or burial assistance.
howToApply: Go to the CSWDO for a one-on-one interview. Bring a Barangay Certification of indigency plus a Medical Certificate from the hospital (medical aid) or the Death Certificate (burial aid), and sign the CSWDO intake form. Approval is signed by the City Mayor.
timing: Walk-in. No fee is listed. Processing is listed at about 10 minutes plus the time for the Mayor's approval (2022 Citizen's Charter).

name: CHED Tulong Dunong Program (TDP)
forWho: Undergraduates (1st–4th year) enrolled at CHED-recognized higher education institutions, with a household income of about ₱400,000 per year or less; prioritizes economically disadvantaged students.
howToApply: Apply through CHED / your school's UniFAST focal person. A DSWD Certificate of Indigency or case study is usually required.
timing: Grant of about ₱7,500 per semester (₱15,000 per year). Now administered directly by CHED (from SY 2026–2027). Application timing varies — check the CHED / UniFAST page for the current cycle.

name: CHED–UniFAST Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES)
provider: CHED — Unified Student Financial Assistance System (UniFAST)
forWho: Students enrolled in SUCs, LUCs, state-run technical-vocational institutions, and eligible private HEIs; prioritized using the DSWD Listahanan / 4Ps list.
howToApply: School-based — apply through your college or university's UniFAST focal person or registrar. There is no single national online deadline.
timing: Rolling and managed per school. Confirm the current cycle and slots with your HEI's UniFAST focal person.

name: DOST-SEI Undergraduate S&T Scholarships
provider: Department of Science and Technology — Science Education Institute (DOST-SEI)
forWho: Incoming college freshmen pursuing priority science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) degrees who pass the DOST-SEI qualifying examination.
howToApply: Apply online at the DOST-SEI scholarship portal during the annual application window, then take the qualifying exam.
timing: Annual. The AY 2026–2027 cycle has concluded (online application Oct–Nov 2025, exam Feb 2026). The next cycle typically opens around October — check the DOST-SEI site.

name: TESDA Scholarship Programs
provider: Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA)
forWho: Individuals seeking free technical-vocational training and national assessment (e.g., TWSP, PESFA, and STEP programs).
howToApply: Enroll through a TESDA-accredited training institution, or inquire at the TESDA office serving Zamboanga del Norte.
timing: Rolling — depends on the course offering and provider. Check TESDA's scholarship page or your local TESDA office for open courses.

name: DSWD AICS — Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situations
provider: Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD)
forWho: Individuals and families in crisis. Covers educational, medical, burial, transportation, and food assistance for those who qualify after assessment.
howToApply: Walk in to the DSWD Field Office / Social Welfare and Development office with a valid ID and supporting documents (e.g., an enrollment assessment for educational aid, hospital bill for medical aid).
timing: Year-round / walk-in, subject to social-worker assessment and availability of funds.
